title: NVIDIA Overlay blackscreen kill
desc: NVIDIA Overlay (GeForce Experience Share) periodically creates fullscreen black windows causing desktop blackout and taskbar animation. Kill the process (nvsphelper64/nvcontainer), not just the HWND.
steps: SYMPTOM: desktop periodically goes black, taskbar animates. Root cause: NVIDIA Overlay (GeForce Experience Share) creates fullscreen HWND covering entire monitor. wkappbot screensaver close detects window but leaves process alive -- NVIDIA respawns it.
DETECT: wkappbot screensaver close logs [SCREENSAVER] wiped ... NVIDIA GeForce Overlay. Or: PowerShell Get-Process NVIDIA Overlay
KILL SESSION: Get-Process NVIDIA Overlay -EA SilentlyContinue
PERMANENT FIX: GeForce Experience -> Settings -> Share -> toggle OFF. Prevents respawn at OS level.

INTEGRATED: screensaver close (v7.3.193+) auto-kills NVIDIA Overlay + nvsphelper64 (ShadowPlay helper) + nvcontainer (GeForce plugin container) when fullscreen black HWND detected. knownOverlayProcs includes all three -- no manual kill needed. Code fix: 66a4f31a5 ScreenSaverStandaloneCommand.cs line 189.
WKAPPBOT_NO_SCREENSAVER=1 disables periodic Eye screensaver scan. Unset to re-enable 2s auto-scan.

SCREENSAVER SELF-WIPE: ScreenSaverOverlay.Lifecycle.cs now calls WipeBlockingOverlays() every 30s while screensaver is visible. This auto-wipes fullscreen (>=75% monitor) non-own windows + NVIDIA Overlay/nvsphelper64/nvcontainer/TextInputHost by name. No manual screensaver close needed while screensaver is active.

BUG FIX 2026-05-27: WipeBlockingOverlays() was sending WM_CLOSE to ALL large visible windows (>=75% screen) every 30s -- including Edge, Chrome, VS Code. Fix: gate PostMessageW(WM_CLOSE) behind if(knownBlocker) check. Non-blocker processes are now only hidden (SetLayeredWindowAttributes+ShowWindow+SetWindowPos) not closed.

DETECTION FIX 2026-05-27: WipeBlockingOverlays old detection was size-only (>=75% screen, no topmost/z-order check) -> false-positived every maximized window (Edge). Root: screensaver is TOPMOST, so only a TOPMOST window can obscure it. Non-topmost windows sit behind and can never block. Fix: for non-knownBlocker, require WS_EX_TOPMOST AND >=50% screen before wipe; WM_CLOSE still gated to knownBlocker only (unknown topmost just hidden). WS_EX_TOPMOST=0x8 added to PInvoke.
